newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mostly lower as cash run-up stalls.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mostly lower as cash run-up stalls.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly lower amid signs the cash market is beginning to weaken after the recent strong advance linked to hot, humid weather in the U.S. Midwest.
Dealers said cash markets started steady early Wednesday but slipped $0.50 lower later in the day in some areas. Cash hogs Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 lower, they said.
They noted sellers of August hogs included Cargill Investor Services, Rand Financial Services and Dean Witter. FIMAT Futures was a noted seller of October.
August hogs closed off 0.325 cent at 80.65 cents a lb.
Other months were 0.275 cent lower to up 0.250 cent.
In hog options there was interest from funds in buying August 80 cents puts and selling 77 cent puts.
Pork belly futures were lower across the board, weakened partly by a higher than expected daily slaughter rate of 338,000 head on Tuesday. Trade estimates had ranged from 320,000 to 335,000 head.
Dealers said Refco was a big seller on August through the day, selling a total of about 150 cars. Hammer Trading was a modest buyer of August.
August bellies closed off 0.350 cent at 82.425 cents.
Other months ended off 0.200 to 0.725 cent.
Dealers said strength in the cash market continued to underpin pork belly futures.
Cash bellies were quoted, as of 1115 CDT Wednesday, for 12- to 14-lb supplies at $90.00 per cwt, up $6.00 since the end of last week, according to USDA.
